correctness.rationale: For same-side vertices indexed i and j, exactly the two matched pairs P_i and P_j contain distance-k distinguishers, so at most one matched pair can be omitted. Equality forces one selected endpoint in every non-omitted pair. For n>=4 every such transversal resolves all pair types. For k>=2 it is automatically dominating; for k=1 its unselected matched mates force at least two selected vertices on each side, and that condition is sufficient. The exhaustive checker agrees for n=5..8 and k=1,2,3.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact optimizer classification and count on a standard distance-transitive family for every sensing range k. It reveals a genuine range transition: the optimum cardinality stays n-1, but the one-step regime excludes precisely the transversals with fewer than two selected vertices on one side, while every transversal becomes feasible from range two onward. This sharpens the general distance-k location-domination theory beyond a routine scalar computation.
